title: Landscape Factors and Seasonal Variation in Stream Fish Assemblages in a Protected Atlantic Forest Area, São Paulo, Brazil
content:
ABSTRACT

Neotropical streams and their fish assemblages are sensitive to both land-use changes and variation between rainy and dry seasons. This study aimed to characterize the fish community and assess the influence of these factors on assemblage structure in three Atlantic Forest streams within a conservation unit. The streams showed differences in habitat characteristics between the rainy and dry seasons. PERMANOVA indicated a significant but relatively small difference in fish assemblage composition between the dry and rainy seasons, with no evidence that seasonal changes differed among streams, while NMDS ordinations illustrated these temporal patterns. Species turnover contributed more to differences between seasons than nestedness. Variance partitioning revealed that landscape variables, namely forest cover and distance from a dam, accounted for a larger unique fraction of variation in fish community structure than spatial or local environmental variables. These findings highlight the importance of landscape context for fish assemblages within conservation units. To support long-term biodiversity conservation, it is essential to protect both habitats within conservation boundaries and the surrounding landscape.
